approachQuestion.prompt:
Separate Alternating Samples

A finite acyclic singly linked list contains sample nodes. Return all nodes originally at positions 1,3,5,... followed by those originally at positions 2,4,6,..., preserving encounter order in each group. Positions are one-based and refer to nodes, not their values. Preserve identities and values; change only next links. Input is head; 0 <= n <= 200000.

Input: A(8) -> B(1) -> C(6) -> D(3) -> E(2). Output: A -> C -> E -> B -> D -> null.
Input: [4,7]. Output: the original order.

Choose a method that satisfies the full contract with the best worst-case running time, breaking time ties by least auxiliary storage.

options.text: Repeatedly move the current second node to the end, continuing until the current node has no successor, without tracking original positions.
options.feedback: For [A,B,C], moving B to the end gives A,C,B; moving the now-second C next gives A,B,C and can continue cycling rather than stopping at the original boundary.

options.text: Walk the original sequence with a parity flag, saving next before detaching each node. Append to an odd-position or even-position tail, toggle parity, then attach the odd tail to the saved even head.
options.feedback: The flag advances with original visits, so positional grouping is independent of values and mutations; tail appends preserve both subsequences.

options.text: Copy all node references into an array and relink odd indices followed by even indices using one-based positions.
options.feedback: This chooses correct positions but retains an unnecessary array of references.

options.text: Group nodes by whether their integer value is odd or even.
options.feedback: For values [8,1], the first node is at an odd position despite holding an even value; value grouping reverses the required order.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (acm-b15-19-target), regardless of your Q1 choice. Here n. Choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Count each node allocation, link access, identity/value comparison and machine-word operation as constant work. Include all temporary collections and call frames; exclude supplied nodes and the final returned output only. Copying or allocating k records costs k operations. No hash-table, amortized-operation or tail-call assumptions are used.

options.explanation: This pair does not describe the fixed method. Every original node is visited, detached and appended once. Inputs of length at least three can require linear rewiring. Two head/tail pairs, a successor and parity flag use constant space; output reuses original nodes without recursion.
